subject: Urgent: log access, redaction and chain-of-custody for outage evidence
messages:
From: Lisa Harper <lisa.harper@acme-payments.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe degradation — need logs & formal evidence for execs

Diego,

We ran into a major degradation this morning (latency spike, ~18% error rate, throughput dropped ~40%) that impacted checkout paths for a subset of users. Our CFO and CISO are asking for an evidence packet for executive briefings and for our internal audit. They specifically asked:

- Full request/response logs (timestamps) for the 06:30–09:30 PDT window
- Authentication/access audit: who pulled or viewed logs during and after the incident
- Any copies of prompt/response content (do these contain cardholder or PII?)
- Chain-of-custody for log exports and retention guarantees (we may need to present this to external auditors)

Can you confirm what you can provide, how soon, and whether we need to sign any data export agreements? We prefer encrypted transfer and an explicit redaction plan for any sensitive content.

Lisa Harper
CIO, Acme Payments

From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Severe degradation — need logs & formal evidence for execs

Diego — thanks for the ping. High-level: we can provide an evidence package but there are a few controls/process items we need to follow for compliance and to protect customer data.

What we can provide (typical incident packet):
- Time-bounded request/response logs (UTC timestamps) within the requested window, exported as gzipped ndjson and a manifest with SHA256 checksums.
- Access audit trail (who listed, downloaded, or accessed logs) from the SIEM and from our internal log-access service, with timestamps and IAM principal ids.
- Runtime metrics (p99 latency, error-rate over time, throughput graphs) and service traces correlated to request ids.
- A redacted sample of raw prompt/response pairs (we can mask PII per your guidance).

Controls/constraints:
- Prompt/response content may include customer data (end-user messages). Exporting full content requires a limited-scope export authorization from the customer (we'll treat this as a data export request).
- We have SOC 2 type II controls: exports are logged, and we can produce a chain-of-custody statement. That will include the export manifest, the SHA256 of files at time of export, and a record of the delivery mechanism (SFTP/secure Drive).
- For legal/audit readiness we will also capture a snapshot of KMS key access logs for the period (if encryption was used) — that may help show who decrypted artifacts in transit.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm the exact timeframe and whether Acme authorizes a content export (full vs. redacted).
2) Choose a transfer mechanism (SFTP with customer key, encrypted Drive with restricted access).
3) We will prepare a chain-of-custody doc and a 1-page executive summary (Priyom can draft).

Target: initial packet within 48 hours of authorization to export content; otherwise we can prepare a metrics & access-only packet in 8–12 hours.

Marcus Lin
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>, Lisa Harper <lisa.harper@acme-payments.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 11:15:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Severe degradation — need logs & formal evidence for execs

Diego / Marcus — technical note on extraction and redaction options: detail below so Acme knows trade-offs.

What we can extract quickly:
- Request/response event logs (request id, route, timestamp, model version, status_code) — stored in hot S3 buckets for 90 days. We can filter by timestamps and request_ids and export as ndjson.
- Traces (sampled) and internal runtime logs (worker-level) — available for 30 days, larger size; we will provide correlated trace ids.
- IAM & SIEM access logs (who did list/get operations on the S3 keys or used the log-viewer) — retention 365 days.

Redaction approach options (pick one):
A) No content export: deliver metrics, access logs, and masked request/response metadata (no prompt/response text). No export authorization needed; 8–12 hour turnaround.
B) Partial content export: export prompt/response pairs but run a scrub that removes or masks any token patterns that look like PAN/SSN/emails (we'll apply regex + ML PII detector). This requires customer sign-off; ~48h to produce and validate.
C) Full content export: deliver raw prompt/response pairs; requires explicit customer approval and an export agreement; we'll do chain-of-custody and storage with restricted access keys. 48–72h depending on size.

Integrity & chain-of-custody steps we will apply for any export:
- Generate an export manifest and compute SHA256 for each artifact.
- Time-stamp export action in our audit log, capture operator account, and store manifest in immutable storage (WORM bucket) for audit.
- Provide checksums and a signed statement of who performed the export and when.

Operational note: some of Acme's requests may trigger support from infra (to snapshot ephemeral cache state or KV cache dumps). Those actions are intrusive and should be scoped with a maintenance window if possible.

Evelyn Hart
Engineering Manager, Runtime & Observability
Redwood Inference

Lisa — quick executive summary and ask: thanks for flagging. Our plan and timelines below.

What we will provide immediately (within 8–12 hours):
- Time-bounded metrics packet: p50/p90/p99 latency, error-rate over time, throughput curves, and a CSV of per-minute aggregates.
- Access audit: SIEM/IAM logs showing who viewed/downloaded any artifacts during and after the incident.

Conditional items (need your confirmation):
- Redacted prompt/response sample (recommended): we will run a scrub to mask likely PII and include a sample export. Target delivery: 48 hours after your confirmation to proceed.
- Full prompt/response export: we can do this but we require an explicit export authorization form (we will send a template). Target delivery: 48–72 hours after signed authorization.

Delivery options: secure SFTP with customer-provided key, or an encrypted Drive folder with ACL restricted to named reviewers. We will also include an export manifest with SHA256 checksums and a chain-of-custody statement.

Please reply with: 1) whether you authorize a redacted sample or full export, and 2) your preferred transfer mechanism. Once we have that, Marcus and Evelyn will start the export flow and Priyom will deliver the executive one-pager.

Thanks — we understand the sensitivity and will treat the packet as high priority.

Diego Fernandez
